messages:
maya (Support): hey team, customer-acme opened a high-severity ticket complaining about a sudden p95/p99 latency regression after we onboarded model-redwood-v2 last night. they say tail latency doubled. linking the incident here for triage. :rotating_light:

alex (Eng-runtime): thanks, maya. do we have numbers? sample endpoints?

maya (Support): they reported for /v1/generate text-gen route: p95 went from ~220ms -> ~780ms, p99 from ~1.2s -> ~2.8s since the v2 rollout at ~1753998000. error rates are low, but latency spike is consistent for requests with long contexts (~3k-6k tokens).

customer-acme: adding our repro payload (sanitized). note we only saw this after you flipped model to model-redwood-v2.
```
{
  "model": "model-redwood-v2",
  "input": "<~3.8k tokens of convo transcript...>",
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```

customer-acme: tail logs show a lot more tokenization tokens than expected (avg token_count ~4.1k vs earlier 2.6k).

alex (Eng-runtime): interesting — v2 included a tokenizer change in the last patch. two hypotheses: 1) tokenizer splits differently increasing model input length -> more KV cache work; 2) attention algorithm fallback for long sequences uses slower kernel path. can someone grab flamegraphs/traces for a few slow requests? @liam @nisha

liam (SRE): grabbing traces now from the p99 samples in the last 2h. initial flame shows 68% time in attention_slow_path and ~20% in tokenization. attaching snippet:
```
Trace sample #1:
  0. tokenization: 210ms
  1. kv-cache population: 320ms
  2. attention_slow_path: 430ms
  3. postprocess/IO: 40ms
```

nisha (ML Ops): that aligns with expected behavior if token counts jumped. tokenizer diffs in PR #448 changed handling of punctuation and some unicode sequences -> could increase tokenization by ~30-50% for long chat transcripts. i can run a local tokenization diff quickly.

alex (Eng-runtime): also check if we accidentally disabled prefix caching for v2 rollout — caching reduces repeated prefix recompute dramatically. maya, did the customer use pinned model or generic routing?

maya (Support): they were on the default routing (no pin). they started seeing regression immediately after our canary moved to 100% traffic.

nisha (ML Ops): ran a quick script on a few sample transcripts. result: token_counts for v1 tokenizer: avg 2,600; v2 tokenizer: avg 3,900 (+50%). that's consistent with their reports.

alex (Eng-runtime): ok that explains extra compute. two mitigation paths: 1) roll back tokenizer change in v2 (fast but reduces improvements), 2) enable tokenizer compatibility layer that maps to v1 tokenization for existing customers, 3) temporarily route long-context requests to model-redwood-v1 or to a slower but optimized long-context runtime with larger KV cache and faster kernels.

liam (SRE): operationally we can create a routing rule to send requests with input_token_count > 3000 to the older runtime/model variant. that would be quick (config change) and buy time. i'll prepare the rule and run limited canary.

maya (Support): customer-acme would prefer a fix on our side rather than switching models, but they're willing to accept routing for now if it reduces latency. can we do an emergency canary to 10% of traffic for long-context to v1?

alex (Eng-runtime): yes. plan: (A) create routing rule by token-count to v1 for >=3200 tokens; (B) rollback tokenizer in next patch if routing doesn't normalize p95; (C) add a compatibility flag in API to preserve old tokenization for pinned customers. i'll own A and B.

nisha (ML Ops): for longer term, we should add an automated tokenization-delta test in our model onboarding. any tokenizer change that increases token count >15% for typical datasets should be flagged and require explicit approval. i can add to the onboarding CI.

liam (SRE): rolled out routing rule to canary (10% long-context traffic) at 1754001800. initial telemetry shows p95 on canaried traffic back to ~240ms, p99 ~1.0s. overall cluster p95 dropped from 780ms -> 430ms within 20 minutes.

customer-acme: can confirm our SLA-reported latency for our flagged calls is back to acceptable range on the canary. thanks.

maya (Support): i'll update customer and keep monitoring. alex, what's ETA on the rollback or compatibility flag?

alex (Eng-runtime): rollback PR queued now, smoke tests running. if green, we can deploy a rollback to prod within ~45min. compatibility flag for API needs a bit more design; estimate ~2 weeks for safe rollout.

nisha (ML Ops): created a draft CI check in onboarding that compares token counts and pushes warning if >15% delta. will open PR this afternoon.

liam (SRE): follow-ups for postmortem: - clarify rollout guardrails for tokenizer changes - add synthetic workloads covering long-context patterns to our perf dashboards - add routing-by-token-count as a standard mitigation playbook. i'll file the incident ticket and link to this thread.

support-bot: noted incident #INC-2025-314 filed, assigned to eng-runtime, sev:P2.

maya (Support): great job everyone. quick notes i'll send to customer: 1) we implemented temporary routing for long-context to earlier runtime (canary live), 2) we are rolling back tokenizer change as a precaution, 3) we will add onboarding controls to prevent this in future. i'll follow up with timeline once rollback completes. :thumbsup:

alex (Eng-runtime): rollback is going out at 1754002310, monitoring now. dropping here, thanks team.

liam (SRE): monitoring post-rollback metrics: cluster p95 back to 230-260ms, p99 ~1.1s. marking incident as mitigated. will still preserve incident for postmortem and remediation tasks.

maya (Support): closing loop with customer in 10, will attach mitigation notes and next steps.

customer-acme: thanks all. appreciate the quick turnaround.

(END OF THREAD)
